**Tiendas Comercial Mexicana S.A. de C.V.**, colloquially known as **La Comercial** and **La Comer**, was a Mexican [hypermarket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypermarket "Hypermarket") group that operated mainly in Mexico City and Central Mexico. It was founded in 1930 and operated by [Controladora Comercial Mexicana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controladora_Comercial_Mexicana "Controladora Comercial Mexicana"). From 2016 to 2018 it was owned and operated by [Soriana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soriana "Soriana"), which also owns Alprecio stores. Comercial Mexicana, including its different store formats, was the third-largest [supermarket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermarket "Supermarket") chain in Mexico as of 2014.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Flor_de_Jamaica.JPG/250px-Flor_de_Jamaica.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flor_de_Jamaica.JPG)

Comercial Mexicana brand Flor de Jamaica (Hibiscus flower)

The first store, which was opened by [Carlos González Nova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Nova "Carlos González Nova") and his father, Antonino González Abascal, in Mexico City in 1930, primarily sold [textile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textile "Textile") products.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-poder-2)

In January 2015 it was announced that [Organización Soriana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soriana "Soriana") would buy Comercial Mexicana stores, from which 118 will be fully owned while 42 would be leased and operated by third parties.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-3)

## Stores

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Stores")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Comercial_Mexicana_Store.jpg/250px-Comercial_Mexicana_Store.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Comercial_Mexicana_Store.jpg)

Comercial Mexicana store in [Zamora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamora,_Michoac%C3%A1n "Zamora, Michoacán"), [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán")

Comercial Mexicana had different retail formats, with the general stores branded as Comercial Mexicana, the larger stores as Mega Comercial Mexicana and its smaller facilities as Bodega Comercial Mexicana. Many of its general stores were connected to a shopping mall with competing businesses surrounding. An example was in [Plaza Río](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_R%C3%ADo_Tijuana "Plaza Río Tijuana") in [Tijuana, Baja California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana,_Baja_California "Tijuana, Baja California"), which had a Comercial Mexicana as an [anchor store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchor_store "Anchor store") but also has a traditional [department store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_store "Department store") and smaller specialty stores selling items that could be purchased in Comercial Mexicana.

## Formats

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Formats")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/3/3f/Soriana2018slogan.png/250px-Soriana2018slogan.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Soriana2018slogan.png)

Last slogan of Comercial Mexicana, shared with Soriana, used in 2018.

From 1962 to 2016, Controladora Comercial Mexicana (currently Grupo LaComer) managed 10 store formats, among which were hypermarkets (Comercial Mexicana), megamarkets (MEGA), self-service warehouses (Bodega Comercial Mexicana), general and premium supermarkets (Sumesa, Fresko and City Market), rural supermarkets (Alprecio), warehouse clubs (Costco) and restaurants (California Restaurants and Beer Factory).

Due to the financial crisis that Controladora Comercial Mexicana went through in 2008, the company decided to gradually dispense with its formats, being Costco the first Comercial Mexicana format to be sold to its US counterpart in 2012, in which said price club entered to the Mexican market through a joint venture in 1991, in which on July 14, 2012, Controladora Comercial Mexicana sold the stake in Costco México to its United States subsidiary Costco Wholesale Corporation for 12,791 million Mexican pesos. Likewise, on August 21, 2014, Controladora Comercial Mexicana sold its Beer Factory and California restaurants to Grupo Gigante for 1,061 million Mexican pesos, which were converted into Toks.

In 2015, with the agreement to sell stores to Soriana, Controladora Comercial Mexicana becomes a subsidiary of Tiendas Soriana; however, it only kept 143 of the 155 stores purchased. However, the process of unification and merger will be staggered, beginning with the joint operation of campaigns, such as that of Julio Regalado. Controladora CM has most of the branches of the original company (143 branches), which operate in the formats Tienda Comercial Mexicana, Bodega Comercial, Mega Comercial and AlPrecio. Between 2016 and 2018, Soriana had the rights to use the original name and logo of "Comercial Mexicana", so the stores that use this badge are those that are managed by the company originally from Torreón and currently based in Monterrey. After this time, these stores were renamed to one of the formats managed by the chain.

As of January 4, 2016, the new company "La Comer" was born, successor to the original company founded in 1930, which intends to manage the four profitable formats of the company, identified as City Market, Fresko, Sumesa and the new entity, known as "La Comer".

Unlike the previous company, it will not offer massive discounts but exclusively in El Buen Fin and its new concept of season of offers, Temporada Naranja (national pulicitaria campaign, successor to Julio Regalado); In addition, the new store will no longer offer clothing or footwear in its new formats. Initially, the company started with 54 units.

## Programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Programs")]

Comercial Mexicana also had programs for children. In exchange for working in stores as bag boys, the children received family support, [tuition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuition_payments "Tuition payments") support and educational supplies, and basic services. The children wore almost-trademark brown uniforms with the orange pelican logo and were expected to be well groomed. They helped most of the customers out of the store and return the carts, which in turn kept the shopping cart thefts low.

## Executives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Executives")]

[Carlos González Nova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Nova "Carlos González Nova"), Comercial Mexicana's co-founder, served as the [chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman "Chairman") of the company's [board of directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_directors "Board of directors") until 1998.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-economista-4)

In 2000 he was responsible for killing musician [Kirsty MacColl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirsty_MacColl "Kirsty MacColl") by striking with a powerboat he was operating recklessly, having entered a restricted area off the coast of [Cozumel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cozumel "Cozumel"), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"). He remained the honorary chairman of Comercial Mexicana until his death on August 19, 2009, at the age of 92.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-economista-4)

In 1998, Guillermo González Nova, younger brother of Carlos, became chairman of the board.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-5)

Carlos González Nova's son, Carlos González Zabalegui, was the last company's [executive chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_chairman "Executive chairman") and [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-economista-4)

**Tiendas Comercial Mexicana S.A. de C.V.**, colloquially known as **La Comercial** and **La Comer**, was a Mexican [hypermarket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypermarket "Hypermarket") group that operated mainly in Mexico City and Central Mexico. It was founded in 1930 and operated by [Controladora Comercial Mexicana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controladora_Comercial_Mexicana "Controladora Comercial Mexicana"). From 2016 to 2018 it was owned and operated by [Soriana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soriana "Soriana"), which also owns Alprecio stores. Comercial Mexicana, including its different store formats, was the third-largest [supermarket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermarket "Supermarket") chain in Mexico as of 2014.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Flor_de_Jamaica.JPG/250px-Flor_de_Jamaica.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flor_de_Jamaica.JPG)

Comercial Mexicana brand Flor de Jamaica (Hibiscus flower)

The first store, which was opened by [Carlos González Nova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Nova "Carlos González Nova") and his father, Antonino González Abascal, in Mexico City in 1930, primarily sold [textile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textile "Textile") products.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-poder-2)

In January 2015 it was announced that [Organización Soriana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soriana "Soriana") would buy Comercial Mexicana stores, from which 118 will be fully owned while 42 would be leased and operated by third parties.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-3)

## Stores

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Stores")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Comercial_Mexicana_Store.jpg/250px-Comercial_Mexicana_Store.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Comercial_Mexicana_Store.jpg)

Comercial Mexicana store in [Zamora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamora,_Michoac%C3%A1n "Zamora, Michoacán"), [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán")

Comercial Mexicana had different retail formats, with the general stores branded as Comercial Mexicana, the larger stores as Mega Comercial Mexicana and its smaller facilities as Bodega Comercial Mexicana. Many of its general stores were connected to a shopping mall with competing businesses surrounding. An example was in [Plaza Río](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_R%C3%ADo_Tijuana "Plaza Río Tijuana") in [Tijuana, Baja California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tijuana,_Baja_California "Tijuana, Baja California"), which had a Comercial Mexicana as an [anchor store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchor_store "Anchor store") but also has a traditional [department store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_store "Department store") and smaller specialty stores selling items that could be purchased in Comercial Mexicana.

## Formats

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Formats")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/3/3f/Soriana2018slogan.png/250px-Soriana2018slogan.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Soriana2018slogan.png)

Last slogan of Comercial Mexicana, shared with Soriana, used in 2018.

From 1962 to 2016, Controladora Comercial Mexicana (currently Grupo LaComer) managed 10 store formats, among which were hypermarkets (Comercial Mexicana), megamarkets (MEGA), self-service warehouses (Bodega Comercial Mexicana), general and premium supermarkets (Sumesa, Fresko and City Market), rural supermarkets (Alprecio), warehouse clubs (Costco) and restaurants (California Restaurants and Beer Factory).

Due to the financial crisis that Controladora Comercial Mexicana went through in 2008, the company decided to gradually dispense with its formats, being Costco the first Comercial Mexicana format to be sold to its US counterpart in 2012, in which said price club entered to the Mexican market through a joint venture in 1991, in which on July 14, 2012, Controladora Comercial Mexicana sold the stake in Costco México to its United States subsidiary Costco Wholesale Corporation for 12,791 million Mexican pesos. Likewise, on August 21, 2014, Controladora Comercial Mexicana sold its Beer Factory and California restaurants to Grupo Gigante for 1,061 million Mexican pesos, which were converted into Toks.

In 2015, with the agreement to sell stores to Soriana, Controladora Comercial Mexicana becomes a subsidiary of Tiendas Soriana; however, it only kept 143 of the 155 stores purchased. However, the process of unification and merger will be staggered, beginning with the joint operation of campaigns, such as that of Julio Regalado. Controladora CM has most of the branches of the original company (143 branches), which operate in the formats Tienda Comercial Mexicana, Bodega Comercial, Mega Comercial and AlPrecio. Between 2016 and 2018, Soriana had the rights to use the original name and logo of "Comercial Mexicana", so the stores that use this badge are those that are managed by the company originally from Torreón and currently based in Monterrey. After this time, these stores were renamed to one of the formats managed by the chain.

As of January 4, 2016, the new company "La Comer" was born, successor to the original company founded in 1930, which intends to manage the four profitable formats of the company, identified as City Market, Fresko, Sumesa and the new entity, known as "La Comer".

Unlike the previous company, it will not offer massive discounts but exclusively in El Buen Fin and its new concept of season of offers, Temporada Naranja (national pulicitaria campaign, successor to Julio Regalado); In addition, the new store will no longer offer clothing or footwear in its new formats. Initially, the company started with 54 units.

## Programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Programs")]

Comercial Mexicana also had programs for children. In exchange for working in stores as bag boys, the children received family support, [tuition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuition_payments "Tuition payments") support and educational supplies, and basic services. The children wore almost-trademark brown uniforms with the orange pelican logo and were expected to be well groomed. They helped most of the customers out of the store and return the carts, which in turn kept the shopping cart thefts low.

## Executives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comercial_Mexicana&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Executives")]

[Carlos González Nova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Nova "Carlos González Nova"), Comercial Mexicana's co-founder, served as the [chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman "Chairman") of the company's [board of directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_directors "Board of directors") until 1998.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-economista-4)

In 2000 he was responsible for killing musician [Kirsty MacColl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirsty_MacColl "Kirsty MacColl") by striking with a powerboat he was operating recklessly, having entered a restricted area off the coast of [Cozumel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cozumel "Cozumel"), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"). He remained the honorary chairman of Comercial Mexicana until his death on August 19, 2009, at the age of 92.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-economista-4)

In 1998, Guillermo González Nova, younger brother of Carlos, became chairman of the board.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-5)

Carlos González Nova's son, Carlos González Zabalegui, was the last company's [executive chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_chairman "Executive chairman") and [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comercial_Mexicana#cite_note-economista-4)

## About us

Grupo La Comer es una empresa 100% mexicana. La compañía opera 79 tiendas de autoservicio, con un área de venta total de aproximadamente 329,033 m2, concentrados principalmente en el área metropolitana de la Ciudad de México en donde se ubica el 40% del total de sus tiendas. Cuenta con dos Centros de Distribución, uno en Guadalajara y otro en la Ciudad de México. Su historia se remonta a 1930 cuando Don Antonino González Abascal y sus hijos Antonino, Carlos, Jaime y Guillermo González Nova fundaron su primera tienda de telas en la Ciudad de México. En 1962 con la apertura de la tienda de San José Insurgentes se inicia la historia de Comercial Mexicana. En el 2002 Comercial Mexicana hizo un replanteamiento de su estrategia comercial orientándose hacia la diferenciación. Este nuevo enfoque dio como resultado el lanzamiento de lo que ha sido su mantra publicitario: ¿…Vas al Súper o a La Comer?, así como la apertura en 2006 de un concepto revolucionario que ha sido fuertemente aceptado: City Market. Siguiendo esta misma filosofía introduce su concepto de supermercado en 2009, bajo el nombre de Fresko. La historia se sigue haciendo día con día, con el trabajo, compromiso y valores de nuestros colaboradores.

## About us

Grupo La Comer es una empresa 100% mexicana. La compañía opera 79 tiendas de autoservicio, con un área de venta total de aproximadamente 329,033 m2, concentrados principalmente en el área metropolitana de la Ciudad de México en donde se ubica el 40% del total de sus tiendas. Cuenta con dos Centros de Distribución, uno en Guadalajara y otro en la Ciudad de México. Su historia se remonta a 1930 cuando Don Antonino González Abascal y sus hijos Antonino, Carlos, Jaime y Guillermo González Nova fundaron su primera tienda de telas en la Ciudad de México. En 1962 con la apertura de la tienda de San José Insurgentes se inicia la historia de Comercial Mexicana. En el 2002 Comercial Mexicana hizo un replanteamiento de su estrategia comercial orientándose hacia la diferenciación. Este nuevo enfoque dio como resultado el lanzamiento de lo que ha sido su mantra publicitario: ¿…Vas al Súper o a La Comer?, así como la apertura en 2006 de un concepto revolucionario que ha sido fuertemente aceptado: City Market. Siguiendo esta misma filosofía introduce su concepto de supermercado en 2009, bajo el nombre de Fresko. La historia se sigue haciendo día con día, con el trabajo, compromiso y valores de nuestros colaboradores.

# La Comer Super Market or La Comer en tu casa

## Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo, Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, México.

[![Image 11](http://www.loscabosguide.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/la-comer-market-cabo-san-lucas-8320-2-300x225.jpg)](http://www.loscabosguide.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/la-comer-market-cabo-san-lucas-8320-2.jpg)

**La Comer en tu casa or La Comer Super Market in Cabo San Lucas**The La Comer Super Market in Cabo San Lucas is not near the hotels. You would need a car or take a taxi or the bus. It is located on the road going towards Todos Santos.

**La Comer Cabo San Lucas**  
 Address: Av. Hidalgo #1055 calle, Calle San Cristóbal,  
 23472 Cabo San Lucas, B.C.S.  
 Phone: 01 624 173 1729  
 La Mega was previously in this location prior to 2015 or 2016.

**La Comer en tu casa San José del Cabo**Address: Blvd. #4650 Col., Mauricio Castro, Zona Hotelera, 23400 San José del Cabo, B.C.S.  
 Hours: Open · 7AM–11PM;Phone: 01 624 142 6435  
 http://www.lacomer.com.mx/

History: **Tiendas Comercial Mexicana S.A. de C.V.**, colloquially known as **La Comercial** or **La Comer**, is a Mexican hypermarket group that operates mainly in Mexico City and Central Mexico. It is owned and operated by Controladora Comercial Mexicana, which also owns Sumesa stores, City Market stores, Alprecio stores and Restaurantes California. Comercial Mexicana, including its different store formats, is the third-largest supermarket chain in Mexico as of 2014. Source: en.wikipedia.org/

**[Fresko La Comer Los Cabos](https://www.loscabosguide.com/fresko-la-comer-cabo-san-lucas/)**

# La Comer Super Market or La Comer en tu casa

## Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo, Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, México.

[![Image 11](http://www.loscabosguide.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/la-comer-market-cabo-san-lucas-8320-2-300x225.jpg)](http://www.loscabosguide.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/la-comer-market-cabo-san-lucas-8320-2.jpg)

**La Comer en tu casa or La Comer Super Market in Cabo San Lucas**The La Comer Super Market in Cabo San Lucas is not near the hotels. You would need a car or take a taxi or the bus. It is located on the road going towards Todos Santos.

**La Comer Cabo San Lucas**  
 Address: Av. Hidalgo #1055 calle, Calle San Cristóbal,  
 23472 Cabo San Lucas, B.C.S.  
 Phone: 01 624 173 1729  
 La Mega was previously in this location prior to 2015 or 2016.

**La Comer en tu casa San José del Cabo**Address: Blvd. #4650 Col., Mauricio Castro, Zona Hotelera, 23400 San José del Cabo, B.C.S.  
 Hours: Open · 7AM–11PM;Phone: 01 624 142 6435  
 http://www.lacomer.com.mx/

History: **Tiendas Comercial Mexicana S.A. de C.V.**, colloquially known as **La Comercial** or **La Comer**, is a Mexican hypermarket group that operates mainly in Mexico City and Central Mexico. It is owned and operated by Controladora Comercial Mexicana, which also owns Sumesa stores, City Market stores, Alprecio stores and Restaurantes California. Comercial Mexicana, including its different store formats, is the third-largest supermarket chain in Mexico as of 2014. Source: en.wikipedia.org/

**[Fresko La Comer Los Cabos](https://www.loscabosguide.com/fresko-la-comer-cabo-san-lucas/)**  
 Tourist Corridor, Cabo San Lucas  
 Scheduled to open Mid November 2021

# La Comer: Cabo’s best shopping secret

What’s your guilty pleasure when you’re on holiday? For some it’s indulging a bit more. For others, it’s partying like it’s 1999. I’m partial to hitting up a good grocery store. Like for hours. Quite possibly the best grocery store in the world is **La Comer**, found in [San Jose del Cabo](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/style-jaunt-cabo/), Mexico. You want bronzed skin AND bargains? Roll up to this little slice of paradise on the Baja Peninsula.

![Image 5: La Comer ](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/La-comer-1.jpg)

So many helpful staff at La Comer can tell you which salsa to buy.

Table of Contents

*   La Comer
*   Cabo Costco

## La Comer

La Comer is conveniently situated at the junction between Highway 1 and Highway 10. You can take either of these highways to the international airport, so if you’re flying in, you’re sure to drive by it. This (formerly a Mega) grocery store sits in the same parking lot as a McDonalds and Starbucks, and is steps away from San Jose’s hotel zone.

It seems like half their customers are American ex-pats, and the store caters to these cash cows. They’ve got volunteers dotted around the store to help you shop.

One quickly pounced on me and she was so knowledgeable about whether cactus tostadas were worth the hype that I kept hunting her down.

I peppered her with questions such as:

*   Do Mexicans drink margaritas out of a can? 
*   Do refried beans taste OK without lard? 

These volunteers can answer all those questions that have been bugging your for years. P.S. expect to receive a look of disgust when asking about omitting lard.

But what can I say? I loooove Mexican food and this mega grocery store is the best spot in the Baja region to snap up all those ingredients.

[![Image 6: La Comer: Cabo’s best shopping secret](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/friends-at-the-grocery-store.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/friends-at-the-grocery-store/)

Me and my bestie.

My gal even ran into the huz and got into a conversation about me, without realizing our mutually close relationships.

Lady: Hello sir, do you have any questions? I’m happy to help.

Huz: Thanks, but I think I’m OK. (Continues shopping for inappropriate T-shirts.)

Lady: No really, it’s fine. I just spent an hour with a Canadian in the hot chocolate aisle.

Huz: Did she ask you a thousand questions?

Lady: Yes!

Editor’s note: I hoping old teenager was just a bad translation for young lady.

### And clothing, too!

With Target and Zellers gone in Canada, I’ve been missing the cheap Cherokee line for kids. They carry it here though, plus a lot of clothing that hasn’t made it past a good translator.

[![Image 7: stupid college T shirts](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/College-What-T-shirt.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/college-what-t-shirt/)

Naturally we bought this shirt and are thinking of giving it to our nephew.

But who could resist such sexy Ts? Not my man. Fast forward a few years and now our daughter proudly wears this shirt.

[![Image 8: target T shirts](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/Camping-T-shirt.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/camping-t-shirt/)

Camping: Meet new friends since 1987. Um, OK!

### Fresh Seafood

Check out the amazing seafood counter below. So much octopus, so little time! The prawns are spectacular. The amount of fresh seafood (and salsas, and other prepared Mexican delights) will make you WANT to cook all through your holiday. OK, maybe not every day, but if you’re headed to the beach (Chileno Bay has a lovely public beach), this is where you’ll want to stop for picnic provisions.

[![Image 9: seafood counter](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/shrimp-and-squid.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/shrimp-and-squid/)

Seafood fresh from the Sea of Cortez.

Ceviche anyone? There are half a dozen varieties on tap every day for your snacking pleasure.

[![Image 10: ceviche counter](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/ceviche-bar.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/ceviche-bar/)

Or maybe it’s salsa? Both are available and made daily.

### Bakery and Tortilla Action

La Comer’s got a full bakery, with freshly made bread and all the treats you’d expect. Handy for those renting a condo is their prepared food section (hello homemade corn tortillas and guacamole!). They even sport a handsome selection of car tires in case you get a flat. Really, this Cabo grocery store has it all – including beach toys like boogie boards, life jackets, etc…

Note: I typically bring back the their homemade tortillas on the plane to Canada and it’s never been an issue. They’re hiding underneath the blue gingham blanket in a cooler (see pic below). Only the locals know its hiding spot!

[![Image 11: Mega tortiallas](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/tortillas-and-guacamole.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/tortillas-and-guacamole/)

Snap up homemade tortillas on your way to the airport. I do!

## Cabo Costco

La Comer rocks for tourists like me keen to snap up American goods at much cheaper prices than we could in the States or Canada. Costco in Cabo is good, too. They have the advantage of being closer to Cabo San Lucas if you’re staying near that area.

Plus, Costco has some sweet views of The Arches from their parking lot. And who can resist the super cheap hot dogs, pizza and sundaes they dish out? Not I! But if given a choice, it’s La Comer (formerly Mega) that I return to time and time again.

Still, at Costco you can stock up on quality booze at cheaper prices if you’re not doing the all-inclusive thing.

Have you ever hit up the grocery stores in Mexico? Have I tempted you?

# La Comer: Cabo’s best shopping secret

What’s your guilty pleasure when you’re on holiday? For some it’s indulging a bit more. For others, it’s partying like it’s 1999. I’m partial to hitting up a good grocery store. Like for hours. Quite possibly the best grocery store in the world is **La Comer**, found in [San Jose del Cabo](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/style-jaunt-cabo/), Mexico. You want bronzed skin AND bargains? Roll up to this little slice of paradise on the Baja Peninsula.

![Image 5: La Comer ](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/La-comer-1.jpg)

So many helpful staff at La Comer can tell you which salsa to buy.

Table of Contents

*   La Comer
*   Cabo Costco

## La Comer

La Comer is conveniently situated at the junction between Highway 1 and Highway 10. You can take either of these highways to the international airport, so if you’re flying in, you’re sure to drive by it. This (formerly a Mega) grocery store sits in the same parking lot as a McDonalds and Starbucks, and is steps away from San Jose’s hotel zone.

It seems like half their customers are American ex-pats, and the store caters to these cash cows. They’ve got volunteers dotted around the store to help you shop.

One quickly pounced on me and she was so knowledgeable about whether cactus tostadas were worth the hype that I kept hunting her down.

I peppered her with questions such as:

*   Do Mexicans drink margaritas out of a can? 
*   Do refried beans taste OK without lard? 

These volunteers can answer all those questions that have been bugging your for years. P.S. expect to receive a look of disgust when asking about omitting lard.

But what can I say? I loooove Mexican food and this mega grocery store is the best spot in the Baja region to snap up all those ingredients.

[![Image 6: La Comer: Cabo’s best shopping secret](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/friends-at-the-grocery-store.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/friends-at-the-grocery-store/)

Me and my bestie.

My gal even ran into the huz and got into a conversation about me, without realizing our mutually close relationships.

Lady: Hello sir, do you have any questions? I’m happy to help.

Huz: Thanks, but I think I’m OK. (Continues shopping for inappropriate T-shirts.)

Lady: No really, it’s fine. I just spent an hour with a Canadian in the hot chocolate aisle.

Huz: Did she ask you a thousand questions?

Lady: Yes!

### And clothing, too!

With Target and Zellers gone in Canada, I’ve been missing the cheap Cherokee line for kids. They carry it here though, plus a lot of clothing that hasn’t made it past a good translator.

[![Image 7: stupid college T shirts](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/College-What-T-shirt.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/college-what-t-shirt/)

Naturally we bought this shirt and are thinking of giving it to our nephew.

But who could resist such sexy Ts? Not my man. Fast forward a few years and now our daughter proudly wears this shirt.

[![Image 8: target T shirts](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/Camping-T-shirt.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/camping-t-shirt/)

Camping: Meet new friends since 1987. Um, OK!

### Fresh Seafood

Check out the amazing seafood counter below. So much octopus, so little time! The prawns are spectacular. The amount of fresh seafood (and salsas, and other prepared Mexican delights) will make you WANT to cook all through your holiday. OK, maybe not every day, but if you’re headed to the beach (Chileno Bay has a lovely public beach), this is where you’ll want to stop for picnic provisions.

[![Image 9: seafood counter](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/shrimp-and-squid.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/shrimp-and-squid/)

Seafood fresh from the Sea of Cortez.

Ceviche anyone? There are half a dozen varieties on tap every day for your snacking pleasure.

[![Image 10: ceviche counter](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/ceviche-bar.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/ceviche-bar/)

Or maybe it’s salsa? Both are available and made daily.

### Bakery and Tortilla Action

La Comer’s got a full bakery, with freshly made bread and all the treats you’d expect. Handy for those renting a condo is their prepared food section (hello homemade corn tortillas and guacamole!). They even sport a handsome selection of car tires in case you get a flat. Really, this Cabo grocery store has it all – including beach toys like boogie boards, life jackets, etc…

Note: I typically bring back the their homemade tortillas on the plane to Canada and it’s never been an issue. They’re hiding underneath the blue gingham blanket in a cooler (see pic below). Only the locals know its hiding spot!

[![Image 11: Mega tortiallas](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/tortillas-and-guacamole.jpg)](https://www.jodyrobbins.com/la-comer/#mega/tortillas-and-guacamole/)

Snap up homemade tortillas on your way to the airport. I do!

## Cabo Costco

La Comer rocks for tourists like me keen to snap up American goods at much cheaper prices than we could in the States or Canada. Costco in Cabo is good, too. They have the advantage of being closer to Cabo San Lucas if you’re staying near that area.

Plus, Costco has some sweet views of The Arches from their parking lot. And who can resist the super cheap hot dogs, pizza and sundaes they dish out? Not I! But if given a choice, it’s La Comer (formerly Mega) that I return to time and time again.

Still, at Costco you can stock up on quality booze at cheaper prices if you’re not doing the all-inclusive thing.

Have you ever hit up the grocery stores in Mexico? Have I tempted you?

Discover Parole Polanco, a vibrant and passionate restaurant in the heart of CDMX. This place evokes the gardens of Tuscany, ideal for celebrating with friends and family. ### [Contramar](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city/contramar)

The artsy-upper crust of the La Condesa neighborhood, hangers-on following the scene, businessmen on lengthy lunches, and a smattering of tourists crowd the tables here. At Contramar, you'll fully understand why lunch is the most important—and longest—meal of the day in Mexico City: By 2 p.m. on Fridays, the brandy and rosé start flowing and lunch turns into multiple rounds of food and drink, smoke breaks on the sidewalk, and a place to be seen. The food is well-executed: tuna tostadas with chipotle mayonnaise and fried leeks, bracing ceviches and aguachiles, whole grilled fish a la talla served with warm tortillas and refried black beans. Dessert is exceptional—a waiter will bring over a tray to show you what's available, but just order as many as you can handle.

### [El Turix](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city-df/el-turix)

This tiny, bare-bones taqueria normally has a line snaking out the front. If there's no space to squeeze in at the tiny steel counter, most people stand out in front to eat. Office workers with their ties thrown over their shoulders, passersby refueling, construction workers stop by here. El Turix excels in the cochinita pibil department—pork rubbed with achiote and citrus, buried underground and slowly smoke-roasted. The meat is topped with a pickled red onion and served on panuchos (lightly fried tortillas filled with black beans), tacos, or tortas. Note that the scarlet-colored achiote seed dyes everything an electric orange, so be careful not to stain your clothes while eating. On the museum circuit in [Polanco](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/what-to-do-in-polanco-mexico-city-our-guide)? Missed your reservation at [Pujol](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city/pujol)? El Turix may actually be the best place to eat in Polanco if you're looking for a quick refuel.

Shiny steel and seafoam green tiles lend a diner-cum-oyster-bar feel to the joint. On a corner, across from their lauded restaurant Martínez, Ultramarinos Delmar is couple, Lucho Martínez and Fernanda Torres' temple to pristine seafood. This restaurant runs on the freshest seafood you can find in Mexico City and leagues of butter and chives. The raw bar with oysters, clams, and a dish of raw kampachi and salmon showered in olive oil and capers cribbed from Swan Oyster Depot, ease you into a meal. There is shrimp cocktail, crab claws, tostadas and crudos. The salt baked fish is perfectly executed, napped in butter. I'd like to be buried in their lobster roll. Like all of Martínez's cooking, the execution is point. There are a few fun wildcards: queso fundido, a melting pool of cheese with a spicy fish chorizo, to be wrapped in flour tortillas and crab cakes whose sweet flesh with no errant shells is reason enough to spend your paycheck.

# 35 Best Restaurants in Mexico City

The stand-out spots in a city that's dense with incredible food.

By [Scarlett Lindeman](https://www.cntraveler.com/contributor/scarlett-lindeman) and [Naomi Tomky](https://www.cntraveler.com/contributor/naomi-tomky)

December 2, 2025

![Image 1: 35 Best Restaurants in Mexico City for Birria Ceviche and Tacos](https://media.cntraveler.com/photos/642b3b135a214d48b40531ca/16:9/w_320%2Cc_limit/Mi%2520Compa%2520Chava.jpg)

In the unfathomably large terrain of Mexico City, there is something excellent to eat on every corner, at every hour. When visiting, a game plan is necessary—as the tacos, quesadillas, and elotes pile up, stomach space quickly becomes a premium. On this list, you’ll find enduring classics, fresh newcomers, international flavors, and taquerias that have been honing their craft through the decades. We suggest selecting a few full-service meals (that will likely require a reservation) and then allow room for everything else that looks appetizing when walking through the streets, puestos, and markets. Mexico City is a multitude, and it satisfies all kinds of tastes.

The bar anchors the space on the left and long, open kitchen showcasing a wood fire grill and the cooks in clean, white aprons hovering over dishes. The vibe is homey but elegant. The menu follows the rhythms of the season and what local farmers are growing. Fish, vegetables, and salads shine. Most dishes are based on classic presentations like salad, ceviches, and grilled meat, for example, but always with a gentle creativity and beautiful plating. A caesar salad is reimagined as a sultry dip for sparklingly fresh lettuces, radishes and herbs. The fish is draped in a corduroy-esqe ribbing of green mango and cucumber. A boy choy kissed by carbon with macadamia nuts and green curry. For the meat-n-potatoes eater, there is a delicious, albeit straightforward, steak, grilled to mid-rare and flanked by a fan of avocado. While a few French touchstones are sprinkled throughout (onion soup with a touch of cumin; buttery escargot served with naan; mussels with rasam) Chanana transports you to the streets and home kitchens of northwestern Indian. ### [Contramar](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city/contramar)

The artsy-upper crust of the La Condesa neighborhood, hangers-on following the scene, businessmen on lengthy lunches, and a smattering of tourists crowd the tables here. At Contramar, you'll fully understand why lunch is the most important—and longest—meal of the day in Mexico City: By 2 p.m. on Fridays, the brandy and rosé start flowing and lunch turns into multiple rounds of food and drink, smoke breaks on the sidewalk, and a place to be seen. The food is well-executed: tuna tostadas with chipotle mayonnaise and fried leeks, bracing ceviches and aguachiles, whole grilled fish a la talla served with warm tortillas and refried black beans. Dessert is exceptional—a waiter will bring over a tray to show you what's available, but just order as many as you can handle.

### [El Turix](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city-df/el-turix)

This tiny, bare-bones taqueria normally has a line snaking out the front. If there's no space to squeeze in at the tiny steel counter, most people stand out in front to eat. Office workers with their ties thrown over their shoulders, passersby refueling, construction workers stop by here. El Turix excels in the cochinita pibil department—pork rubbed with achiote and citrus, buried underground and slowly smoke-roasted. The meat is topped with a pickled red onion and served on panuchos (lightly fried tortillas filled with black beans), tacos, or tortas. Note that the scarlet-colored achiote seed dyes everything an electric orange, so be careful not to stain your clothes while eating. On the museum circuit in [Polanco](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/what-to-do-in-polanco-mexico-city-our-guide)? Missed your reservation at [Pujol](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city/pujol)? El Turix may actually be the best place to eat in Polanco if you're looking for a quick refuel.

### [Ultramarinos Demar](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city/ultramarinos-demar)

Shiny steel and seafoam green tiles lend a diner-cum-oyster-bar feel to the joint. On a corner, across from their lauded restaurant Martínez, Ultramarinos Delmar is couple, Lucho Martínez and Fernanda Torres' temple to pristine seafood. This restaurant runs on the freshest seafood you can find in Mexico City and leagues of butter and chives. The raw bar with oysters, clams, and a dish of raw kampachi and salmon showered in olive oil and capers cribbed from Swan Oyster Depot, ease you into a meal. There is shrimp cocktail, crab claws, tostadas and crudos. The salt baked fish is perfectly executed, napped in butter. I'd like to be buried in their lobster roll. Like all of Martínez's cooking, the execution is point. There are a few fun wildcards: queso fundido, a melting pool of cheese with a spicy fish chorizo, to be wrapped in flour tortillas and crab cakes whose sweet flesh with no errant shells is reason enough to spend your paycheck.

### [Masala & Maíz](https://www.cntraveler.com/restaurants/mexico-city-df/masala-y-maiz)

With a cookbook about to drop in 2026, a Chef’s Table Netflix episode, a fresh Michelin star, and a move to a more spacious location in Centro, Masala & Maíz is maturing into a true fine-dining restaurant. The menu is mostly new, but stellar standbys remain, including shell-on prawns in ghee infused with vanilla and esquites, traditional Mexican corn kernels with fresh coconut milk, ginger, turmeric, and topped with purslane. The restaurant's captivating mix of Mexican technique and Indian touchstones has been refined, and the restaurant is all grown up in a sexy space that reflects its evolution. Look for the whole roasted kuku poussin and a vinegary mussel dish with salsa balchao, plus an exciting cocktail menu and coffee, to boot.

**Eataly** is a chain of large Italian [food halls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_hall "Food hall") comprising a variety of restaurants, food and beverage counters, bakery, retail stores, and a cooking school. Eataly was founded by [Oscar Farinetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Farinetti "Oscar Farinetti"), an entrepreneur formerly involved in the [consumer electronics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_electronics "Consumer electronics") business, and collaborates with [Slow Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow_Food "Slow Food").

## Origin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Origin")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Eataly_New_York_City_September_2010.jpg/250px-Eataly_New_York_City_September_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eataly_New_York_City_September_2010.jpg)

The first of three Eataly branches in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), seen in September 2010

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/EatalyBrasilSP.jpg/250px-EatalyBrasilSP.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EatalyBrasilSP.jpg)

Eataly in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo"), Brazil, now closed[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Baselice-2)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Eatily_in_CF_Sherway_Garden_2023.jpg/250px-Eatily_in_CF_Sherway_Garden_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eatily_in_CF_Sherway_Garden_2023.jpg)

Eataly in [Sherway Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherway_Gardens "Sherway Gardens"), [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Canada

In January 2007, Italian businessman Oscar Farinetti opened the first location of Eataly,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-atlantic1-3) converting a closed vermouth factory in the [Lingotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingotto "Lingotto") district of [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin "Turin"). Easily accessible via the [Lingotto metro station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingotto_(Turin_Metro) "Lingotto (Turin Metro)"), the establishment has been described by _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ as a "megastore" that "combines elements of a bustling European open market, a Whole-Foods-style supermarket, a high-end [food court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_court "Food court") and a New Age learning center."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-nyt07far-4) Farinetti planned early on that additional stores would open elsewhere in Italy and in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") with help of investor chef [Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-nyt07far-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The first Eataly location in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan") was established in the [Toy Center Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy_Center "Toy Center") near [Madison Square Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Park "Madison Square Park").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-nynotebook-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-fox-6) It is over 50,000 square feet (4,600 m 2) in size,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-7) and opened with a large amount of press coverage on August 31, 2010.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-la_stampa1-11) Mayor [Michael Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg") and Eataly investor chef [Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali") attended the opening, praising Eataly for creating 300 new jobs.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-12) Two weeks after opening, there were still lines extending down Fifth Avenue to get into the store.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-suntimes-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-platt-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-16) The New York Eataly had originally been planned for a smaller space near [Rockefeller Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Center "Rockefeller Center").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-changes-17)

The chain has additional locations in Italy and a few in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-toronto1-18) In 2012, Eataly opened its largest megastore, in Rome in the abandoned Air Terminal building near [Ostiense Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roma_Ostiense_railway_station "Roma Ostiense railway station"). There is an Eataly at Rome's [Fiumicino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci%E2%80%93Fiumicino_Airport "Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport") airport, and in the Porto Antico area in [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa").

In January 2013, Eataly announced a partnership with [MSC Cruises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSC_Cruises "MSC Cruises") to open two restaurants on _[MSC Preziosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSC\_Preziosa "MSC Preziosa")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-19) Eataly was also added to _[MSC Divina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSC\_Divina "MSC Divina")_.

On December 2, 2013, Eataly opened a new location at 43 E. Ohio St. in Chicago, on a 63,000-square-foot (5,900 m 2) retail space,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-20) making it the largest Eataly in the US. The cost of the Chicago venture is estimated at $20 million. On March 18, 2014, Eataly opened its big 5,000-square-metre (54,000 sq ft) store in Piazza XXV Aprile in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan").

The founder Oscar Farinetti received the _America Award_ of the [Italy-USA Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy-USA_Foundation "Italy-USA Foundation") in 2013. On December 16, 2014, Eataly opened the first store at [Zorlu Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zorlu_Center "Zorlu Center") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"). On May 19, 2015, Eataly opened its first store in the southern hemisphere in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Baselice-2) On November 26, 2015, Eataly opened in [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), making it the first location in Germany.

2016 saw [Andrea Guerra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Guerra_(businessman) "Andrea Guerra (businessman)") become CEO of Eataly. Guerra had previously served as the CEO of eyewear giant [Luxottica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxottica "Luxottica") from 2004 to 2014.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-:1-21)

In June 2016, it was announced that an Eataly location would open in 2018 at the [Park MGM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_Resort_and_Casino "Monte Carlo Resort and Casino") casino in Las Vegas (formerly the Monte Carlo).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-22) Eataly would fill approximately 40,000 square feet (3,700 m 2) on the southern edge of the resort and The Park-facing side would become the main pedestrian entrance into the Park MGM casino.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-24)

In July 2016, Eataly announced a [Downtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Manhattan "Downtown Manhattan") location at the [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(2001%E2%80%93present) "World Trade Center (2001–present)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-25)

In November 2016, a 45,000-square-foot (4,200 m 2) Eataly location opened in the [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston")[Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Tower "Prudential Tower"), replacing an existing food court after extensive renovations.

In October 2017, Eataly Century City location opened at the newly remodeled $1-billion [Westfield Century City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfield_Century_City "Westfield Century City") Mall in Los Angeles County. Covering 67,000 square feet (6,200 m 2), Eataly LA surpassed Eataly Chicago to become the largest Eataly in the US.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-26)

On February 17, 2018, Eataly opened its 40th location in Stockholm, Sweden. The operation occupies 32,300 square feet (3,000 m 2) in a former movie theater in the heart of Stockholm's shopping district.

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Eataly_at_King_of_Prussia_Mall.jpeg/250px-Eataly_at_King_of_Prussia_Mall.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eataly_at_King_of_Prussia_Mall.jpeg)

Eataly at the [King of Prussia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Prussia_(shopping_mall) "King of Prussia (shopping mall)") mall in [King of Prussia, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Prussia,_Pennsylvania "King of Prussia, Pennsylvania")

In April 2019, Eataly opened its first location in Paris, France. It is located in the center of the French capital in [the Marais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marais "The Marais") neighborhood, between the [Place des Émeutes-de-Stonewall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_des_%C3%89meutes-de-Stonewall "Place des Émeutes-de-Stonewall") (Stonewall Riots Square) and the rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie, in [Le Marais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Marais "Le Marais") ([4th arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_arrondissement_of_Paris "4th arrondissement of Paris")).

The autumn of 2019 saw Guerra depart Eataly for an executive leadership position at [LVMH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LVMH "LVMH"). Guerra's replacement was Nicola Farinetti, son of founder Oscar Farinetti.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-:1-21)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-27)

On November 13, 2019, Eataly opened a 50,000-square-foot (4,600 m 2) store in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Canada, in the [Manulife Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manulife_Centre "Manulife Centre") on Bloor Street.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-28)

On December 9, 2020, Eataly opened a 40,000-square-foot (3,700 m 2) store in Dallas, Texas, at NorthPark Center.

Eataly announced the dissolution of its franchise in Moscow due to the Russian military invasion of Ukraine on 30 March 2022.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-29)

In September 2022, the UK investment firm Investindustrial VII LP became Eataly's owner by acquiring a majority 52% of its shares for 200 million euros.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-:0-30)

On November 2, 2023, Eataly opened its second Toronto location at [Sherway Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherway_Gardens "Sherway Gardens") shopping mall with 25,000 square feet (2,300 m 2) of space.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Sherway-31) On May 30, 2024, it opened its third Toronto location at [Shops at Don Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shops_at_Don_Mills "Shops at Don Mills") with 9,800 square feet (910 m 2).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-32) A fourth Toronto location opened on November 25, 2025, at the [Eaton Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eaton_Centre "Eaton Centre"), spanning 25,000 square feet (2,300 m 2) across two levels. It is also the only city with at least four locations after New York City.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-33)

Eataly severed ties with its São Paulo store in December 2023. The franchise holder continued to operate the store without permission until August 2025 when a court order closed the branch.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Baselice-2)

## Name

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Name")]

The name Eataly was coined by Celestino Ciocca, a [brand strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_strategy "Brand strategy")[consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consultant "Consultant") who has worked for [Texas Instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Instruments "Texas Instruments") and [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young"). He first registered Eataly as a [domain name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name "Domain name") on February 23, 2000, and as a [trademark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trademark "Trademark") in June 2000. Ciocca sold (by his family company) all his rights to the name to Natale Farinetti on February 3, 2004, by public deed _repertorio n° 96538 – raccolta n° 11510_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Animal welfare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Animal welfare")]

In 2022, Eataly signed the [European Chicken Commitment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Chicken_Commitment "European Chicken Commitment") (ECC), thereby committing to implement several improvements in chicken living standards and humane slaughter practices by 2026. [[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-35)

## Controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Controversy")]

[Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali"), previously a minority owner and founder of Eataly, is now no longer attached to the company following sexual misconduct allegations against him. Eataly pulled all products bearing his likeness two days after the allegations surfaced in 2017.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-36)

**Eataly** is a chain of large Italian [food halls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_hall "Food hall") comprising a variety of restaurants, food and beverage counters, bakery, retail stores, and a cooking school. Eataly was founded by [Oscar Farinetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Farinetti "Oscar Farinetti"), an entrepreneur formerly involved in the [consumer electronics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_electronics "Consumer electronics") business, and collaborates with [Slow Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow_Food "Slow Food").

In January 2007, Italian businessman Oscar Farinetti opened the first location of Eataly,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-atlantic1-3) converting a closed vermouth factory in the [Lingotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingotto "Lingotto") district of [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin "Turin"). Easily accessible via the [Lingotto metro station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingotto_(Turin_Metro) "Lingotto (Turin Metro)"), the establishment has been described by _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ as a "megastore" that "combines elements of a bustling European open market, a Whole-Foods-style supermarket, a high-end [food court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_court "Food court") and a New Age learning center."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-nyt07far-4) Farinetti planned early on that additional stores would open elsewhere in Italy and in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") with help of investor chef [Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-nyt07far-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The first Eataly location in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan") was established in the [Toy Center Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy_Center "Toy Center") near [Madison Square Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Park "Madison Square Park").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-nynotebook-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-fox-6) It is over 50,000 square feet (4,600 m 2) in size,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-7) and opened with a large amount of press coverage on August 31, 2010.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-la_stampa1-11) Mayor [Michael Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg") and Eataly investor chef [Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali") attended the opening, praising Eataly for creating 300 new jobs.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-12) Two weeks after opening, there were still lines extending down Fifth Avenue to get into the store.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-suntimes-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-platt-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-16) The New York Eataly had originally been planned for a smaller space near [Rockefeller Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Center "Rockefeller Center").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-changes-17)

The chain has additional locations in Italy and a few in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-toronto1-18) In 2012, Eataly opened its largest megastore, in Rome in the abandoned Air Terminal building near [Ostiense Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roma_Ostiense_railway_station "Roma Ostiense railway station"). There is an Eataly at Rome's [Fiumicino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci%E2%80%93Fiumicino_Airport "Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport") airport, and in the Porto Antico area in [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa").

In January 2013, Eataly announced a partnership with [MSC Cruises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSC_Cruises "MSC Cruises") to open two restaurants on _[MSC Preziosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSC\_Preziosa "MSC Preziosa")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-19) Eataly was also added to _[MSC Divina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSC\_Divina "MSC Divina")_.

On December 2, 2013, Eataly opened a new location at 43 E. Ohio St. in Chicago, on a 63,000-square-foot (5,900 m 2) retail space,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-20) making it the largest Eataly in the US. The cost of the Chicago venture is estimated at $20 million. On March 18, 2014, Eataly opened its big 5,000-square-metre (54,000 sq ft) store in Piazza XXV Aprile in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan").

The founder Oscar Farinetti received the _America Award_ of the [Italy-USA Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy-USA_Foundation "Italy-USA Foundation") in 2013. On December 16, 2014, Eataly opened the first store at [Zorlu Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zorlu_Center "Zorlu Center") in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"). On May 19, 2015, Eataly opened its first store in the southern hemisphere in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Baselice-2) On November 26, 2015, Eataly opened in [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"), making it the first location in Germany.

2016 saw [Andrea Guerra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Guerra_(businessman) "Andrea Guerra (businessman)") become CEO of Eataly. Guerra had previously served as the CEO of eyewear giant [Luxottica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxottica "Luxottica") from 2004 to 2014.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-:1-21)

In June 2016, it was announced that an Eataly location would open in 2018 at the [Park MGM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_Resort_and_Casino "Monte Carlo Resort and Casino") casino in Las Vegas (formerly the Monte Carlo).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-22) Eataly would fill approximately 40,000 square feet (3,700 m 2) on the southern edge of the resort and The Park-facing side would become the main pedestrian entrance into the Park MGM casino.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-24)

In July 2016, Eataly announced a [Downtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Manhattan "Downtown Manhattan") location at the [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(2001%E2%80%93present) "World Trade Center (2001–present)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-25)

In November 2016, a 45,000-square-foot (4,200 m 2) Eataly location opened in the [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston")[Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Tower "Prudential Tower"), replacing an existing food court after extensive renovations.

In October 2017, Eataly Century City location opened at the newly remodeled $1-billion [Westfield Century City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfield_Century_City "Westfield Century City") Mall in Los Angeles County. Covering 67,000 square feet (6,200 m 2), Eataly LA surpassed Eataly Chicago to become the largest Eataly in the US.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-26)

On February 17, 2018, Eataly opened its 40th location in Stockholm, Sweden. The operation occupies 32,300 square feet (3,000 m 2) in a former movie theater in the heart of Stockholm's shopping district.

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Eataly_at_King_of_Prussia_Mall.jpeg/250px-Eataly_at_King_of_Prussia_Mall.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eataly_at_King_of_Prussia_Mall.jpeg)

Eataly at the [King of Prussia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Prussia_(shopping_mall) "King of Prussia (shopping mall)") mall in [King of Prussia, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Prussia,_Pennsylvania "King of Prussia, Pennsylvania")

In April 2019, Eataly opened its first location in Paris, France. It is located in the center of the French capital in [the Marais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marais "The Marais") neighborhood, between the [Place des Émeutes-de-Stonewall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_des_%C3%89meutes-de-Stonewall "Place des Émeutes-de-Stonewall") (Stonewall Riots Square) and the rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie, in [Le Marais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Marais "Le Marais") ([4th arrondissement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_arrondissement_of_Paris "4th arrondissement of Paris")).

The autumn of 2019 saw Guerra depart Eataly for an executive leadership position at [LVMH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LVMH "LVMH"). Guerra's replacement was Nicola Farinetti, son of founder Oscar Farinetti.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-:1-21)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-27)

On November 13, 2019, Eataly opened a 50,000-square-foot (4,600 m 2) store in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Canada, in the [Manulife Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manulife_Centre "Manulife Centre") on Bloor Street.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-28)

On December 9, 2020, Eataly opened a 40,000-square-foot (3,700 m 2) store in Dallas, Texas, at NorthPark Center.

Eataly announced the dissolution of its franchise in Moscow due to the Russian military invasion of Ukraine on 30 March 2022.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-29)

In September 2022, the UK investment firm Investindustrial VII LP became Eataly's owner by acquiring a majority 52% of its shares for 200 million euros.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-:0-30)

On November 2, 2023, Eataly opened its second Toronto location at [Sherway Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherway_Gardens "Sherway Gardens") shopping mall with 25,000 square feet (2,300 m 2) of space.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Sherway-31) On May 30, 2024, it opened its third Toronto location at [Shops at Don Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shops_at_Don_Mills "Shops at Don Mills") with 9,800 square feet (910 m 2).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-32) A fourth Toronto location opened on November 25, 2025, at the [Eaton Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eaton_Centre "Eaton Centre"), spanning 25,000 square feet (2,300 m 2) across two levels. It is also the only city with at least four locations after New York City.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-33)

Eataly severed ties with its São Paulo store in December 2023. The franchise holder continued to operate the store without permission until August 2025 when a court order closed the branch.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-Baselice-2)

## Name

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Name")]

The name Eataly was coined by Celestino Ciocca, a [brand strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_strategy "Brand strategy")[consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consultant "Consultant") who has worked for [Texas Instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Instruments "Texas Instruments") and [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young"). He first registered Eataly as a [domain name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name "Domain name") on February 23, 2000, and as a [trademark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trademark "Trademark") in June 2000. Ciocca sold (by his family company) all his rights to the name to Natale Farinetti on February 3, 2004, by public deed _repertorio n° 96538 – raccolta n° 11510_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Animal welfare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Animal welfare")]

In 2022, Eataly signed the [European Chicken Commitment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Chicken_Commitment "European Chicken Commitment") (ECC), thereby committing to implement several improvements in chicken living standards and humane slaughter practices by 2026. [[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-35)

## Controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Eataly&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Controversy")]

[Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali"), previously a minority owner and founder of Eataly, is now no longer attached to the company following sexual misconduct allegations against him. Eataly pulled all products bearing his likeness two days after the allegations surfaced in 2017.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eataly#cite_note-36)
